title: Concurrent Acquisition Coherence Under Moderate (Realistic) Contention
motivation: E24 tested naive-vs-fenced acquisition coherence only under sustained, adversarially maximal contention (all three resources flipped concurrently as fast as HTTP round-trips allow), where the fenced double-collect mechanism never delivered a result within its retry bound. This leaves open whether the fenced mechanism is USEFUL at a realistic background-mutation rate, or only ever fail-safe. This experiment reuses E24's exact mechanism, resources, and coherence oracle, adding a bounded inter-toggle delay to the mutator so it represents plausible occasional configuration drift (an order of magnitude slower than a full fenced acquisition round) rather than adversarial saturation.

mutator.description: Identical concurrent all-three-resource-flip mutator as E24, with a fixed inter-tick delay inserted between toggle rounds so toggles occur at a bounded rate rather than as fast as possible.

coherence_definition: Identical to E24: an acquired combination is COHERENT iff there exists an instant during the trial at which every queried resource's ground-truth value (reconstructed from the mutator's timestamped log) equals the value returned for it.
notes: Preregistered post-hoc extension (E28), run outside the locked v8.1.1 package and outside all other v9/E21/E23-E27 evidence. Reuses E24's namespace/ConfigMaps without modifying E24's own frozen protocol or results.
